newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends easy, gilts await auction result.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends easy, gilts await auction result.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday at 5.25-5.5 percent, down from opening quotes of 5.5-6.25 percent, dealers said.
"There was resistance from borrowers at higher levels," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Further, liquidity is expected to improve tomorrow as the repos is reversed tomorrow."
The Reserve Bank of India conducted a four-day repos auction on February 1 in which it mopped up 36.65 billion rupees. The second leg of the transaction takes effect on Friday.
A fresh four-day auction takes place later on Thursday.
"There was little trade (in securities) today as market participants are awaiting the results at today's auction before taking positions," said a dealer.
The volume of trades on the NAtional Stock Exchange fell to 1.10 billion rupees from Wednesday's 1.73 billion.
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Thursday at 103.10 rupees against its last traded price of 103.05 while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock improved to 103.24 from 103.18.
Dealers said treasury bills maturing in April were traded at 7.55 percent against last traded yield of 7.45 percent.
There were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit, dealers said.
